DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks

paper.arxiv.2607.07946

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Complete primary manuscript and pinned creator README/LICENSE were independently read by three separate AI invocations, and all 16 paper-scoped claims bind actual author, source-verifier and adversarial source-content review records at their exact scientific digests. Software engineer task/environment/test authorship and peer quality controls, original 113-task/91-repository fixed-harness study, scored-run/exclusion/error denominators, uncertainty and fallible second-opinion judge remain qualified. Structural engineering horizon is not a human-time estimate. Original PIE and later README Pier/v1.1 describe separate inspected versions, not assumed equivalent results. No additional family, current provider ranking, task/container/code execution, upstream rights clearance or frozen-core eligibility is inferred.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks · benchmark task: DeepSWE contains 113 tasks across 91 active public repositories in TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript and Rust; its repository-selection rules require at least 500 GitHub stars and a permissive open-source license.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.deepswe.paper.corpus-and-repository-selection.v2

  • Each task pins an immutable base commit, and the median repository contributes one task.
  • The corpus targets substantial repository-scale implementation, with smaller single-file edits and bug-localization work under-represented.

DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks · paper method: DeepSWE evaluates 16 model-and-reasoning-effort configurations under mini-swe-agent with a shared prompt and single bash tool, pinned to commit adfe20233d456104c38c3129161b54f0fd39f2c7.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks · documents: DeepSWE uses binary functional rewards without partial credit and does not score code readability, idiomatic style, maintainability, performance or documentation.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.deepswe.paper.functional-binary-scope.v1

  • A nearly complete patch and one that never compiles can both fail; equal pass results do not establish equal code quality or readiness for a maintainer to merge.
  • The paper also excludes non-coding uses such as explanation, code review and interactive developer collaboration, with genuinely ambiguous requests largely outside its construction.

DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks · evaluates: In the paper's DeepSWE experiment, GPT-5.5 at xhigh reasoning effort has the highest reported pass@1, 70.0%, with a run-to-run 95% interval of 67.2-72.9%.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.deepswe.paper.reported-headline-result-scope.v2

  • The result uses the fixed mini-swe-agent setup, the 113-task corpus and the stated infrastructure-exclusion and timeout rules, rather than a native coding-product evaluation.
  • The paper cautions that its single-harness scores do not rank overall model quality or production coding products, and its intervals omit task-selection uncertainty.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks · paper method: DeepSWE reports 95% intervals as pass@1 plus or minus 1.96 times the standard deviation of the roughly four benchmark-run scores divided by the square root of the number of runs.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.deepswe.paper.run-to-run-uncertainty.v1

  • These intervals measure rerun noise on the same 113 tasks and omit uncertainty from the choice of tasks; the authors also warn that about four runs can give deceptively narrow intervals.
  • For GPT-5.5, the paper compares the run-to-run interval of 67.2-72.9% with a wider pooled Wilson interval of 65.6-74.1%, illustrating differing uncertainty conventions.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks · paper method: DeepSWE defines pass@1 as the equally weighted average of each task's scored-rollout pass fraction, while pass@4 is the fraction of 113 tasks with at least one success among up to four attempts.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.deepswe.paper.task-macroaverage-and-four-attempts.v1

  • The macro-average gives each task equal weight even when exclusions leave different numbers of scored attempts.
  • For tasks with fewer than four remaining scored runs, the at-least-one-success indicator can understate a full four-attempt pass@4 budget.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks · documents: In the published DeepSWE comparison, a GPT-5.5 judge disagrees with executable verifier decisions on 10 of 735 DeepSWE runs, 1.4%, versus 256 of 789 SWE-Bench Pro runs, 32.4%.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.deepswe.paper.verifier-disagreement-and-judge-limit.v1

  • The sample uses 30 randomly selected tasks per benchmark, nine of the 16 evaluated configurations and three attempts per task; the xhigh judge reads the trajectory, reference solution, task and verifier output.
  • Rates are over all reviewed runs, not conditioned on verifier passes or failures; the DeepSWE total comprises two judge-assessed false positives and eight false negatives.
  • The authors call this disagreement rather than ground-truth verifier error, flag possible GPT-5.5 self-preference, and withhold the exact judge prompt; executable verifiers remain the leaderboard graders.
